title: August and the Promise
premise: Casper Montrose, a marine biologist who fled their hometown twenty years ago after a betrayal that cost their brother's life, has built a careful existence counting sea turtles on a quiet island. When their mother demands they attend the family reunion with a partner, Casper recruits Wren Okafor, a charming ferry mechanic and the sibling of the person they wronged, to pose as their date for one weekend. But the fake romance turns real by dessert, and as the season's last ferry approaches, Casper must choose between confessing the truth that could destroy both families or letting Wren sail away believing a lie. In the end, Casper tells the truth at the reunion, loses and regains Wren's trust, and the book closes with the two of them staying past the last train, choosing each other over the safety of leaving.
about_author: Sebastian Brightwater is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who now writes love stories set in coastal towns where the tides keep better secrets than people do. Their work explores the quiet courage it takes to be known.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. On the island, Casper logs the season's final turtle nests, revealing a life built on routine and avoidance. A letter from their mother arrives demanding attendance at the family reunion—with a partner. The emotional beat: comfortable loneliness cracking under old obligation.

chapters.title: The Ferry Mechanic
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Wren Okafor fixes the ferry's engine while Casper waits, and their banter is immediate and disarming. Casper learns Wren is the younger sibling of Danny Okafor—the friend who died the night everything fell apart. The beat: attraction shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: An Indecent Proposal Over Coffee
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper asks Wren to be their fake date for the reunion weekend, offering free room and board. Wren, needing a place to stay after an eviction, agrees with a smirk. The beat: a deal struck with equal parts hope and self-deception.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over a shared dinner, they set ground rules: no real feelings, no questions about the past, leave on the last ferry Sunday. Wren breaks rule two immediately with one question Casper refuses to answer. The beat: intimacy disguised as logistics.

chapters.title: Arriving Home
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The reunion begins at the Montrose family's coastal inn. Wren watches Casper shrink around their family, performing a version of themselves Wren doesn't believe. The beat: protective tenderness toward a stranger's mask.

chapters.title: The Mother's Toast
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper's mother toasts the 'happy couple' while Casper's aunt pointedly mentions Danny Okafor's name. Wren's hand finds Casper's under the table—steady, warm, unasked. The beat: the past intruding, the fake date becoming real refuge.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. After dessert, they escape to the dock. Wren confesses they've never felt this easy with anyone; Casper almost tells the truth about Danny, then swallows it. They share a first real kiss. The beat: joy arriving exactly where it was forbidden.

chapters.title: The Brother's Room
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper visits the sealed bedroom of their brother Elias, who drowned the night Casper drove him to the cliffs to meet Danny. Flashback fragments surface. Wren finds Casper there and holds them. The beat: grief surfacing through the cracks of the lie.

chapters.title: Sunday's Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The reunion ends. Wren boards the last ferry as agreed, but at the rail, turns back—and Casper is already running down the pier. Wren misses the boat deliberately. The beat: the first open choice of feeling over contract.

chapters.title: Staying Past the Last Train
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren stays on the island with no job and no exit plan, fixing boats for cash. They fall into domestic rhythm—morning surveys, evening cooking. Casper keeps deflecting questions about Danny. The beat: borrowed happiness on an unpaid debt.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Wren finds an old photograph in Casper's truck: Casper, Elias, and Danny at the cliffs, dated the week of the drowning. Wren's face changes. They don't confront Casper—yet. The beat: suspicion blooming in a warm house.

chapters.title: Danny's Letters
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren visits their estranged parents and finds Danny's unsent letters, which describe a secret meeting at the cliffs with 'C.M.' the night he died. Wren reads them twice. The beat: the fake date's foundation turning to ash in their hands.

chapters.title: The Confrontation at the Survey Site
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confronts Casper on the beach at dawn: 'You were there when my brother died, and you hired me to play house.' Casper can't deny it. Wren walks out. The beat: betrayal stacked on grief, love curdling into accusation.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Full flashback: twenty years ago, Casper drove Elias and Danny to the cliffs; a storm surge took Elias; Casper fled before the truth could be told—that Danny wasn't to blame, and neither was Casper, but Casper let Danny's family believe the worst. The beat: the full price of survival revealed.

chapters.title: The Empty Nest Count
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper works alone, hollowed out, and realizes the small safe steps were a slow drowning of their own. Their mother, having overheard the confrontation, asks for the truth. The beat: the bottom of the arc—nothing left to hide behind.

chapters.title: The Reunion, Again
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At the family's end-of-season gathering, Casper stands and tells everyone the truth about the night Elias died—clearing Danny's name and their own cowardice. The room fractures; their mother weeps; some family walks out. The beat: climax—the truth spoken at last, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: Wren's Verdict
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reads Casper's letter recounting everything, including the part Danny's letters never knew: Casper went back for Elias and failed. Wren grieves the brother and the liar at once. The beat: the question of whether truth is enough to rebuild on.

chapters.title: The Off-Season Ferry
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren decides to leave on the final ferry after all—not from anger, but because they need to choose Casper freely, not from pity. Casper lets them go, saying only, 'I'll be here when the season turns.' The beat: love that releases instead of clings.

chapters.title: Letters to the Water
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Winter arrives; Casper writes letters to Elias and to Danny's memory, finally forgiving themselves, and mails a copy to Wren without expecting an answer. They keep the lighthouse lamp lit for the returning turtles. The beat: solitary reckoning becoming quiet peace.

chapters.title: The First Ferry of Spring
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren returns on the first ferry of the new season, having spent the winter with their parents, telling them the truth about Danny. They carry Danny's letters to give Casper. The beat: forgiveness earned, not granted.

chapters.title: The Promise
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. On the beach at the old cliffs, they bury Danny's letters beside a marker for Elias and make a promise aloud: no more leaving, no more lies. Wren takes Casper's hand in front of the rising tide. The beat: grief and love fused into commitment.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Epilogue, one year later: the reunion comes again, and this time Casper arrives with Wren, no pretense, no rules. The last train passes the island's station with both of them still on the sand. The beat: staying, at last, as the truest form of love.
